land.text: Tây Ninh Province, where the NLF was founded at Tân Lập village on 20 December 1960, and Bến Tre, where the uprisings that began in January 1960 created 'liberated zones'

predecessors.note: The NLF arose inside the Republic of Vietnam (1955-1975); the land it first held is the researcher's reading of two places the Viet Cong page names. The PRG page gives 'Republic of Vietnam' as its predecessor state.

land.text: all of South Vietnam: the infobox area is 173,809 km2 in 1975; Cliopatria's 1966 outline of the Republic is 180,020 km2

successors.note: 2 July 1976: 'the Republic of South Vietnam and the Democratic Republic of Vietnam constitutionally merged' (PRG page); the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is the infobox successor.

capitals.name: Tây Ninh (NLF headquarters, Tân Lập village)
capitals.note: Viet Cong infobox: headquarters Tây Ninh 1960-66. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Tây Ninh town, not the village.

capitals.name: Memot (NLF/COSVN headquarters, Cambodia)
capitals.note: Viet Cong infobox: Memot 1966-72; 'COSVN retreated to Mimot in Cambodia' after January 1966. Not on the PRG page's capital list; coordinates from the Memot District page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memot_District). The PRG page's own list puts Tây Ninh 1969-72, which is why Memot is cut at 1969.

capitals.name: Lộc Ninh
capitals.note: PRG infobox: Lộc Ninh 1972-1973; coordinates from the Lộc Ninh district page (11.84325 N, 106.59103 E). The Viet Cong infobox lists Lộc Ninh 1972-75.

capitals.name: Cam Lộ
capitals.note: PRG infobox: Cam Lộ 1973-1975; coordinates from the Cam Lộ district page (16.817 N, 106.950 E).

capitals.name: Saigon-Gia Dinh (Ho Chi Minh City)
capitals.note: PRG infobox: Saigon-Gia Dinh 1975-1976; 'the PRG moved into government offices there' after 30 April 1975 (Viet Cong page).

correction.text: Tây Ninh Province, where the NLF was founded at Tân Lập village on 20 December 1960, and Bến Tre, where the uprisings that began in January 1960 created 'liberated zones'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The NLF's two named holds: Tây Ninh (founding, COSVN's first base 'near the Cambodian border') and Bến Tre ('liberated zones' from January 1960). The Vietnam War page says only that 'a third of the population was soon living in areas of communist control' and, late 1963, that the Viet Cong 'retain de facto control of much of the countryside'; no page maps it, so the real hold was wider and unmapped (soft).

correction.text: Tây Ninh Province alone: the PRG's capital 1969-1972 and the COSVN base area

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Viet Cong page: 'End of 1969: little communist-held territory remained in the rural lowlands of Cochin China' (Bến Tre is dropped); the PRG page puts its capital at Tây Ninh 1969-1972. Tây Ninh alone is the only named hold.

union.text: the Cam Lộ area of northern Quảng Trị, the PRG's seat from 1973 (the Easter Offensive page: ARVN took 'the majority of Quang Tri province', leaving the north-west to the PAVN)
the Lộc Ninh area, taken on 7 April 1972 and the PRG's capital 1972-73

correction.text: the territory the PAVN held at the end of the Easter Offensive that the PRG administered: the Cam Lộ area, the Lộc Ninh area and the western fringe of III Corps at Tây Ninh; the page says 'the western fringes of the II and III Corps sectors' and 'in total around 10% of the country' without a boundary

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the Easter Offensive (30 March to 22 October 1972) the PAVN 'did hold territory at the end of the offensive as well as the western fringes of the II and III Corps sectors. In total around 10% of the country.' Boundary not on the page; the Cam Lộ and Lộc Ninh circles are the two PRG seats and Tây Ninh stands for the III Corps fringe. Confidence low; the 1973 'land grab' that enlarged the hold is on the Ho Chi Minh campaign page without a region.

correction.text: all of South Vietnam: the infobox area is 173,809 km2 in 1975; Cliopatria's 1966 outline of the Republic is 180,020 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. From 30 April 1975 the PRG held all of South Vietnam: 'After the Fall of Saigon on 30 April 1975, the PRG assumed power in South Vietnam' (PRG page); infobox area 173,809 km2 against 180,020 km2 for the Cliopatria Republic of Vietnam 1956 outline (ratio 0.97), so the outline is used.

region.text: Tây Ninh Province, where the NLF was founded at Tân Lập village on 20 December 1960, and Bến Tre, where the uprisings that began in January 1960 created 'liberated zones'

ledger.note: 1960: the National Liberation Front is founded on 20 December at Tân Lập village in Tây Ninh Province. 'North Vietnam established the National Liberation Front (NLF) on December 20, 1960, at Tân Lập village' in Tây Ninh; 'uprisings beginning in Bến Tre' in January 1960 'created liberated zones'. The pages give the village and the province, not a boundary.

region.text: Tây Ninh Province, where the NLF was founded at Tân Lập village on 20 December 1960, and Bến Tre, where the uprisings that began in January 1960 created 'liberated zones'

ledger.note: 1960: the countryside is fought for from the start. After COSVN ordered a coordinated uprising 'a third of the population was soon living in areas of communist control'; the page names no places, so the zone is the two places the Viet Cong page names.

1966: the NLF headquarters withdraws to Memot in Cambodia. 'After Australian troops found a COSVN tunnel complex in January 1966, COSVN retreated to Mimot in Cambodia.' The infobox gives Memot 1966-72.

1969: the NLF becomes the Provisional Revolutionary Government on 8 June. The PRG 'was formed on 8 June 1969, by the Democratic Republic of Vietnam'; the convention met 'off Route 22 in Cambodia's Fishhook region'.
1969: the PRG's capital is Tây Ninh (PRG infobox, 1969-1972). DISAGREEMENT: the Viet Cong infobox keeps the NLF headquarters at Memot to 1972.

region.text: Bến Tre, the one Mekong lowland zone the page names

ledger.note: 1969: the Mekong lowlands are lost. 'End of 1969: little communist-held territory remained in the rural lowlands of Cochin China'; Bến Tre is the one lowland zone the page names, so it is the zone dropped.

region.text: the Lộc Ninh area, taken on 7 April 1972 and the PRG's capital 1972-73

ledger.note: 1972: the PAVN takes Lộc Ninh on 7 April, in the Easter Offensive ('before collapsing under the attack on 7 April'); the page says Lộc Ninh or An Lộc 'would be proclaimed as the capital of the Provisional Revolutionary Government', and the PRG page lists Lộc Ninh as capital 1972-73.
1972: the PRG capital moves from Tây Ninh to Lộc Ninh (PRG infobox: Lộc Ninh 1972-1973).

region.text: Quảng Trị Province: 'Quảng Trị City ... fell to PAVN forces on 2 May'

ledger.note: 1972: Quảng Trị City falls to the PAVN on 2 May; the advance was 'halted on 5 May at the Mỹ Chánh Line'. The page credits the PAVN, the PRG administration is the researcher's reading.

minus.text: the Cam Lộ area of northern Quảng Trị, the PRG's seat from 1973 (the Easter Offensive page: ARVN took 'the majority of Quang Tri province', leaving the north-west to the PAVN)

region.text: Quảng Trị Province less the Cam Lộ area: 'South Vietnam eventually gaining control of the city in September as well as the majority of Quang Tri province'

ledger.note: 1972: the ARVN retakes Quảng Trị, the Citadel 'finally taken on 16 September', and 'the majority of Quang Tri province'; the north-west around Cam Lộ stays PAVN/PRG.
1973: the PRG capital moves to Cam Lộ in Quảng Trị (PRG infobox: Cam Lộ 1973-1975). The Viet Cong infobox keeps Lộc Ninh to 1975; the PRG page is followed.

region.text: Phước Long Province: the fighting 'continued until 6 January 1975, after which the town became the first provincial capital permanently seized by PAVN'

ledger.note: 1975: Phước Long falls on 6 January, the first provincial capital the PAVN holds. The page names the old province; Bình Phước is its modern successor and also holds Lộc Ninh.

region.text: Darlac Province: 'Darlac Province in its entirety then fell under North Vietnamese control' after Buôn Ma Thuột (battle from 10 March, city taken 18 March)

ledger.note: 1975: Buôn Ma Thuột falls on 18 March and Darlac Province with it. [Reviewer se-04-x: confidence 3 to 2; the Ho Chi Minh campaign page dates the city ('capturing the city of Buôn Ma Thuột on 18 March') but does not name the province.]

region.text: Pleiku and Kon Tum, abandoned by order of President Thiệu; the evacuation column moved out on 16 March

ledger.note: 1975: the Central Highlands are abandoned in mid-March: 'Pleiku and Kon Tum were to be abandoned'. The page does not date the PAVN entry, so the month is the retreat's.

region.text: Huế, captured 'by the end of March'

ledger.note: 1975: Huế falls by the end of March (the page gives no day).

region.text: Đà Nẵng: the PAVN 'swept in on 29 March'

ledger.note: 1975: Đà Nẵng falls on 29 March.

region.text: all of South Vietnam: the infobox area is 173,809 km2 in 1975; Cliopatria's 1966 outline of the Republic is 180,020 km2

ledger.note: 1975: South Vietnam surrenders on 30 April. The South Vietnamese government was forced 'to surrender on 30 April 1975'; Xuân Lộc (Long Khanh) had fallen after the week-long fighting that began on 8 April, and the final attack began on 26-27 April. The page does not date the provinces between Đà Nẵng and Saigon, so the rest of the South is gained here.
1975: the PRG enters Saigon: 'the PRG moved into government offices there' after 30 April (the PRG page lists Saigon-Gia Dinh 1975-1976).

region.text: Tây Ninh Province, where the NLF was founded at Tân Lập village on 20 December 1960, and Bến Tre, where the uprisings that began in January 1960 created 'liberated zones'

ledger.note: 1975: the war ends with the surrender of 30 April; the original contest zone passes wholly to the PRG.

region.text: all of South Vietnam: the infobox area is 173,809 km2 in 1975; Cliopatria's 1966 outline of the Republic is 180,020 km2

ledger.note: 1976: the PRG merges with the north on 2 July. 'On 2 July 1976, the Republic of South Vietnam and the Democratic Republic of Vietnam constitutionally merged.'

region.text: all of South Vietnam: the infobox area is 173,809 km2 in 1975; Cliopatria's 1966 outline of the Republic is 180,020 km2

ledger.note: 1976: the PRG ends and its land is the Socialist Republic of Vietnam's (PRG infobox: successor Socialist Republic of Vietnam; Viet Cong page: 'the PRG was dissolved' in July 1976).

wars.name: Vietnam War

zones.text: Tây Ninh Province, where the NLF was founded at Tân Lập village on 20 December 1960, and Bến Tre, where the uprisings that began in January 1960 created 'liberated zones'

wars.outcome: PRG and North Vietnamese victory: Saigon surrendered on 30 April 1975 and the two Vietnams merged on 2 July 1976.
wars.note: The page extract was cut off before 1969; only the 1960 and 1963 control statements were read. From 1961 the NLF zone is a soft insurgent hold with no mapped boundary.

wars.name: Tet Offensive
wars.outcome: 'In January and February 1968, some 80,000 VC struck more than 100 towns'; the offensive did not trigger the general uprising the VC hoped for and moved no border.

wars.name: Easter Offensive

zones.text: the Lộc Ninh area, taken on 7 April 1972 and the PRG's capital 1972-73
Quảng Trị Province, taken 2 May and mostly lost again by 16 September 1972

wars.outcome: The PAVN held Lộc Ninh and the north-west of Quảng Trị and the western fringes of II and III Corps, about 10 percent of the country; the ARVN retook Quảng Trị City on 16 September.

wars.name: Ho Chi Minh campaign

zones.text: all of South Vietnam: the infobox area is 173,809 km2 in 1975; Cliopatria's 1966 outline of the Republic is 180,020 km2

wars.outcome: 13 December 1974 to 30 April 1975: Phước Long, Buôn Ma Thuột, Huế, Đà Nẵng, Xuân Lộc and Saigon fall; the Republic of Vietnam surrenders.

certainty.note: A guerrilla zone with no recorded boundary; the pages name only Tây Ninh, Bến Tre, Lộc Ninh and the Cam Lộ area.
From 30 April 1975 the PRG holds the Republic of Vietnam's outline.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x (Cliopatria lacks it); the counterpart slug is the one the republic-of-vietnam and democratic-republic-of-vietnam dossiers already use. Pages give almost no territorial extent: the PRG page has none, the Viet Cong page only the founding places and the end-1969 statement, the Easter Offensive page 'around 10%' without a boundary, so 1961-1971 and 1972-1974 are soft readings at confidence 2. Unmapped for want of a page: the 1960s countryside ('a third of the population', 'much of the countryside'), the 1973 ceasefire-in-place land grab, the 1974 ARVN recovery of 15 percent of the land, the NLF/PAVN bases in Cambodia and Laos (PAVN occupation, in the DRV dossier), the Paris Peace Accords of 27 January 1973 (the PRG signed 'as an independent entity'; the Ho Chi Minh campaign page and the PRG caption date it garbled, so it is not a ledger event). Disagreements: Memot versus Tây Ninh 1966-72 and Cam Lộ versus Lộc Ninh 1973-75 between the Viet Cong and PRG infoboxes; PRG page follows. No ruler strip: the PRG page gives two co-heads (Nguyễn Hữu Thọ, chairman of the Consultative Council 6 June 1969-2 July 1976; Huỳnh Tấn Phát, chairman of the government 8 June 1969-2 July 1976). Gazetteer names wanted: Cam Lộ and Lộc Ninh as places (currently coordinate radii), Xuân Lộc. The infobox area 173,809 km2 (1975) was compared with the Republic of Vietnam outline (ratio 0.97). Page budget: 5 content pages plus 3 coordinate pages.
